decisions.title: Public API Resource Paths and Versioning
decisions.question: Which stable public HTTP resource hierarchy and version boundary will expose LIST_PUBLIC_PRODUCTS and GET_PUBLIC_PRODUCT_BY_SLUG?
decisions.why_human: Route hierarchy and versioning are externally observable and become a compatibility commitment.

options.summary: Versioned Storefront resource hierarchy with list and slug-detail beneath a public Storefront identifier.
options.contract: Use /api/v1/storefronts/{storefront_slug}/products and /api/v1/storefronts/{storefront_slug}/products/{public_slug}; web paths remain /catalog and /catalog/{public_slug} in the same Storefront context.
options.impact: Storefront isolation is explicit in the URI and API evolution has a visible v1 boundary.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Longer URLs and future Storefront identifier changes require explicit compatibility handling.

options.summary: Versioned catalog resources with Storefront supplied by a required public request header.
options.contract: Use /api/v1/catalog/products and /api/v1/catalog/products/{public_slug}; require X-Storefront-Slug and reject missing or ambiguous context without fallback.
options.impact: Short resource URLs but Storefront scope is less visible and browser/cache behavior depends on header variance.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Higher risk of omitted-header leakage and more complex caching and evidence.

options.summary: Unversioned Storefront-scoped product resources.
options.contract: Use /storefronts/{storefront_slug}/products and slug detail without an explicit API version segment.
options.impact: Simpler initial surface with no declared version namespace.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Future incompatible evolution lacks an agreed compatibility boundary.

decisions.recommendation_rationale: It makes Storefront isolation and compatibility versioning directly testable without inventing authentication.
non_inferences: No route implementation is authorized by recommendation alone.

decisions.title: Storefront Context, Locale Input and Localization Fallback
decisions.question: How are requested Storefront and locale resolved, and what happens when localized mandatory content is unavailable?
decisions.why_human: Context resolution controls isolation; fallback changes customer-visible content and mandatory-field eligibility.

options.summary: Resolve a validated BCP 47 requested locale, then the configured Storefront default locale.
options.contract: Storefront comes only from the route/header mechanism selected by DEC-001; locale comes from Accept-Language. Exact supported locale wins, then Storefront default. If mandatory localized fields remain absent, exclude from list and use uniform not-found for detail; optional fields remain omitted.
options.impact: Deterministic fallback supports usable localized browsing while retaining mandatory-field guarantees.
options.rejection_tradeoff: A fallback response may not use the caller's first requested locale and must expose the resolved content locale without internal state.

options.summary: Require an exact supported requested locale and never fall back.
options.contract: Unsupported or incomplete mandatory localized content excludes list entries and produces uniform not-found detail; optional fields are omitted.
options.impact: Strong locale predictability and no cross-locale substitution.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Catalog availability can vary sharply by locale and empty states become more common.

options.summary: Ignore caller locale preference and always use the configured Storefront default locale.
options.contract: All list/detail content uses one Storefront locale; no request-level locale selection is exposed in VS001.
options.impact: Smallest contract and fixture matrix.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Does not provide caller-driven localization despite localized source obligations.

decisions.recommendation_rationale: It preserves Storefront isolation, provides deterministic localization and fails closed when mandatory public content cannot be resolved.
non_inferences: No inference of content from Product name.

decisions.title: List Pagination and Deterministic Ordering
decisions.question: What list-window and stable ordering contract prevents duplicates, omissions and nondeterministic evidence?
decisions.why_human: Pagination and ordering are observable response semantics and affect future clients.

options.summary: Opaque cursor pagination over deterministic public_slug then opaque canonical identity ordering.
options.contract: Default page size 20, maximum 100; cursor encodes no public internal IDs and represents the last public_slug plus opaque public identity in the evaluated Storefront snapshot.
options.impact: Stable traversal under a fixed snapshot and no offset drift.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Cursor encoding and snapshot continuity add implementation and test complexity.

options.summary: Offset/limit pagination with the same deterministic public ordering.
options.contract: Default limit 20, maximum 100; order by public_slug then opaque public identity; return total only if independently resolved in the same snapshot.
options.impact: Simple client navigation and test setup.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Concurrent changes can shift offsets unless the implementation adds snapshot/version semantics.

options.summary: Return the complete eligible seeded Storefront catalog under an explicit maximum size.
options.contract: No pagination parameters; fail closed if eligible count exceeds 100; deterministic public_slug then opaque identity ordering remains mandatory.
options.impact: Smallest VS001 API and evidence surface.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Creates an early hard size limit and requires a future public-contract change for growth.

decisions.recommendation_rationale: It provides deterministic evidence and better growth compatibility without exposing storage identity.

decisions.title: Public Wire Schema, Error Envelope and Media Representation
decisions.question: Which stable JSON projection and media representation carries the approved fields and uniform error without exposing internal state?
decisions.why_human: Field names, envelopes and media indirection are public compatibility commitments.

options.summary: Explicit versioned DTOs inside data/meta envelopes with a minimal public error object.
options.contract: List returns {data:[PublicProductListItem],meta:{page}} and detail returns {data:PublicProductDetail}; primary_image is {url,alt}; uniform failure is {error:{code:'PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND',message:'Product not found'}} with HTTP 404 and no reason fields.
options.impact: Clear extension points and independently schema-validatable list/detail/error projections.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Adds envelope nesting and commits exact public field names.

options.summary: Bare array/object success payloads with a top-level public error object.
options.contract: List returns PublicProductListItem[]; detail returns PublicProductDetail; primary image remains a url/alt object; error is {code:'PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND',message:'Product not found'}.
options.impact: Minimal payload and client parsing.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Future pagination and metadata additions require headers or a breaking envelope change.

options.summary: Resource documents with type/id/attributes and errors collections.
options.contract: Represent public Product identity as resource id, approved fields as attributes, media as a public attribute object and uniform not-found as one errors entry carrying PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND.
options.impact: Standardized resource shape and extensibility.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Higher ceremony and risk of accidentally exposing relationship or internal metadata not approved for VS001.

decisions.recommendation_rationale: It keeps the approved field boundary explicit while supporting pagination and schema evidence without supplier/internal relationships.
non_inferences: No promotion, tax, inventory or cart properties.
No internal reason in body or headers.

decisions.title: Public Slug and Opaque Canonical Identity Persistence
decisions.question: How are Storefront-scoped stable slugs and opaque canonical public identities persisted without exposing storage or Supplier identifiers?
decisions.why_human: Identifier lifecycle affects public compatibility, privacy and uniqueness constraints.

options.summary: Persist slug on the Storefront Catalog entry and a separate immutable UUIDv7 public Product identity.
options.contract: Enforce unique(storefront_id,public_slug), approved lowercase ASCII kebab grammar, immutable-after-publication slug in VS001 and unique UUIDv7 public_product_id unrelated to database sequence or Supplier reference.
options.impact: Direct Storefront lookup and sortable opaque public identity with explicit constraints.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Slug history or future cross-Storefront canonical URLs require a later approved model.

options.summary: Use a dedicated public identifier table with Storefront-scoped slug and immutable UUIDv4 Product identity.
options.contract: Resolve slug through a typed identifier row linked to Storefront Catalog entry; disable alias/history rows in VS001; enforce uniqueness and grammar at database and application boundaries.
options.impact: Separates public identifier lifecycle from catalog projection and leaves controlled expansion space.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Additional relation and resolver complexity for features explicitly excluded from VS001.

options.summary: Derive slug from Product name and encode internal identity in the public identifier.
options.contract: Generate identifiers from display content plus reversible storage identity.
options.impact: Avoids a dedicated public identifier lifecycle.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Conflicts with stable locale-neutral slug and no-internal-identity rules; retained only as an explicit rejectable alternative.

decisions.recommendation_rationale: It directly enforces Storefront uniqueness, stable slug and opaque canonical identity with the smallest approved VS001 model.
non_inferences: No direct lookup by database or Supplier ID.

decisions.title: VS001 Relational Persistence and Integrity Model
decisions.question: Which PostgreSQL representation preserves canonical Product authority, typed catalog projections, publication and price lifecycles?
decisions.why_human: Table boundaries, reference ownership and constraints become durable data-lifecycle commitments.

options.summary: Normalized typed tables for canonical Product, versions, catalog roles, entries, publication validation/window, localized public content, media and Storefront price.
options.contract: Use foreign keys and object-type-safe relations; unique current Product Version per Product, unique Storefront Catalog entry per Product/context, non-overlapping active publication rows where required, amount as exact decimal minor-unit-compatible value, ISO currency constraint, and no Supplier cost in public projection tables.
options.impact: Strong reference integrity and independently queryable evidence for every eligibility predicate.
options.rejection_tradeoff: More migrations, joins and fixture setup than aggregate storage.

options.summary: Relational identity/lifecycle tables with source-defined public Product specification stored as validated JSONB.
options.contract: Keep Product, version, catalog, publication and price normalized; store conditional public specification in schema-versioned JSONB validated at write/publication boundaries.
options.impact: Retains lifecycle integrity while avoiding premature columns for conditional attributes.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Database-level field constraints and query evidence for conditional attributes are weaker and require schema validators.

options.summary: Persist one denormalized Storefront public catalog document containing identity, publication, price and display data.
options.contract: Treat the document as a projection rebuilt from canonical entities; it may never become canonical Product authority.
options.impact: Simple read path and snapshot consistency.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Greater stale-projection and dangling-reference risk, with harder independent evidence of typed ownership.

decisions.recommendation_rationale: It protects canonical lifecycle and typed references while avoiding unsupported mandatory columns for conditional Product specification fields.
non_inferences: No Supplier procurement or inventory schema.
No rewrite of the accepted commissioning baseline migration.

decisions.title: Forward Migration, Seed and Controlled Fixture Ownership
decisions.question: How are durable schema migrations separated from deterministic disposable VS001 fixtures?
decisions.why_human: Seed placement changes data lifecycle, cleanup safety and production compatibility.

options.summary: Add one or more forward-only schema migrations and a separate deterministic VS001 fixture loader/cleanup owner.
options.contract: Migrations contain schema only; fixtures use stable semantic fixture keys plus a run ownership token, run only in disposable local/test PostgreSQL, and cleanup deletes only owned rows/resources on success and failure.
options.impact: Clean lifecycle separation and safe reproducible evidence without production seed coupling.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Requires dedicated fixture tooling and ownership validation.

options.summary: Place deterministic VS001 Product/Catalog fixtures directly in forward migrations.
options.contract: Migration data becomes durable database history and is not removed by test cleanup.
options.impact: Migration verification immediately has browseable data.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Conflates schema and test data, complicates production use and violates disposable fixture ownership.

options.summary: API startup creates missing VS001 schema data and fixtures.
options.contract: Startup performs idempotent data creation before serving requests.
options.impact: Low separate-tooling burden.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Creates hidden runtime writes, weakens migration authority and risks persistent environment contamination.

decisions.recommendation_rationale: It reuses commissioning's forward-only migrations and disposable Docker ownership without turning fixtures into durable business seed data.
non_inferences: No fixed container name or shared volume deletion.
No runtime evidence is created in this decision pack.

decisions.title: Eligibility Evaluation Snapshot, Clock, Publication Validation and Price Resolution
decisions.question: What request-scoped consistency model binds publication, reference, validation and price evidence for list/detail?
decisions.why_human: Temporal and concurrent resolution choices can change observable eligibility and list/detail equality.

options.summary: Capture one UTC evaluation instant and resolve all eligibility, publication, validation and price facts in one PostgreSQL repeatable-read snapshot.
options.contract: Inject the clock for controlled boundary tests; list cursor retains snapshot identity or fails closed when continuation cannot preserve it; detail resolves one coherent snapshot; publication validation PASS record and base price amount/currency must be current in that snapshot.
options.impact: Strong independent evidence and no mixed-version list/detail response within a request.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Longer transactions or snapshot continuation mechanisms require careful limits.

options.summary: Capture one UTC instant but use read-committed queries with explicit entity/version stamps and retry on inconsistency.
options.contract: Every resolver receives the same evaluation instant; compare Product Version, publication-validation and price revision identifiers before serialization; retry once then fail closed.
options.impact: Short transactions with explicit optimistic consistency evidence.
options.rejection_tradeoff: More resolver logic and retry behavior; failure semantics become observable under churn.

options.summary: Read a prevalidated materialized Storefront catalog snapshot with immutable snapshot/version identity.
options.contract: Publication and price changes create a new snapshot; list/detail expose only one active validated snapshot and never fall back to raw unresolved state.
options.impact: Fast coherent reads and simple list/detail comparison.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Introduces projection freshness, activation and rebuild lifecycle not otherwise required by VS001.

decisions.recommendation_rationale: It most directly proves the accepted publication-window, validation, reference and price predicates with a controlled clock and coherent evidence.
non_inferences: No claim that list and a later independent detail request share historical state unless the selected contract explicitly carries snapshot identity.

decisions.title: Public/Internal Separation, Correlation and Audit Redaction
decisions.question: How will API/UI/data evidence correlate without exposing internal eligibility, Supplier, cost or storage details?
decisions.why_human: Correlation exposure and logging policy define a security and privacy boundary.

options.summary: Generate a server correlation UUID per request, expose only that opaque value, and use allowlisted structured internal audit fields.
options.contract: Return X-Correlation-Id on success and uniform failure; log correlation id, semantic operation, Storefront public identity and internal reason code only in protected evidence; redact Supplier identity/reference, cost, credentials, storage paths and raw request secrets; never vary public outcome by reason.
options.impact: Enables API/UI/data traceability and internal cause audit with an explicit public allowlist.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Public correlation headers add a compatibility and abuse-monitoring surface.

options.summary: Generate correlation identity internally but expose no correlation field or header publicly.
options.contract: Browser/API evidence correlates through test-harness capture and protected logs; public bodies and headers contain no correlation identity.
options.impact: Smallest public disclosure surface.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Black-box support and API/UI/database evidence correlation are harder and depend on privileged test instrumentation.

options.summary: Accept a constrained client correlation token and echo it after validation, otherwise generate a server value.
options.contract: Allow only bounded ASCII opaque tokens; never place the token into queries or unescaped logs; public response echoes only the validated token.
options.impact: Supports end-to-end caller tracing.
options.rejection_tradeoff: Adds spoofing, log-injection and privacy risk plus more security tests.

decisions.recommendation_rationale: It makes required API/UI/data correlation independently observable while preserving uniform public not-found and strict redaction.
non_inferences: No Supplier or cost logging authorization.
No production retention policy or deployment authorization.
